newsitem.title: UK: Lead/zinc TC talks move in favour of miners.
newsitem.headline: Lead/zinc TC talks move in favour of miners.

text.p: The closure of Anvil Range's Faro lead/zinc mine, announced last week, has shifted the balance in annual treatment cost talks towards miners, Macquarie Equities Ltd said.
Anvil is to suspend mining for three months from December 20, due to weak lead and zinc prices.

"The closure is likely to have a significant impact on the negotiations for 1997 zinc and lead treatment charges (TCs) which are currently underway between miners and smelters," Macquarie said in its latest weekly report.
Before this development lead TCs appeared almost certain to rise by at least $10 a tonne, with some smelters looking for a $25/tonne increase.
A rise is still likely, as smelters do not have much difficulty in obtaining concentrates, Macquarie said.

"However, increased demand from Chinese smelters, which are reported to be trying to raise output, together with reduced production at Faro, could virtually eliminate the surplus, restricting the rise in lead TCs to $10/tonne or less."
In zinc, an expected surplus in concentrates this year has failed to materialise, due to increased Chinese demand and a series of mine closures and delays.

Before Anvil Range's announcement miners were looking for cuts of $10/20/tonne, while smelters opened with bids of a $7/10 increase. So far, zinc smelters are still resisting calls for big cuts in TCs.
However, recent spot market deals support the miners case, with the small amount of spot tonnage being sold at very low TCs in the $160/164 range.
Macquarie's expectation is for 1997 annual TCs to be settled around the $180/tonne level, against 1996's $190/tonne.
